visual_review.review_method: Visual inspection of both contact sheets (32 frames each), original-resolution frames at 41.2, 41.5 and 41.9 seconds, plus trajectory continuity checks. Not real-time browser playback.
findings: Complete grasp, transport, release and withdrawal sequence visible across whole-room frames.
Detail camera shows edge overhang, gravity-driven tipping, fall and liquid film after impact.
No obvious temporal trails seen in sampled moving-arm boundaries.
Navigation step cumulative rotation about 89.8 degrees; no full-turn loop.
limitations: Whole-room camera briefly occludes the falling bottle behind the robot; synchronized detail camera covers release and fall.
Robot base partly cropped at the initial source position.
Liquid is an uncalibrated reduced-order rendering, not CFD.

visual_review.review_method: Visual inspection of full-room and detail contact sheets (24 frames each), dense release frames 44.1–45.0 s and final state at 66.9 s, plus trajectory continuity checks. Not real-time browser playback.
findings: Grasp, transport, centre placement and withdrawal visible.
Bottle stays upright on the tabletop after gripper separation through the final frame.
No visible floor liquid film and no monitored physical or modeled liquid event.
Navigation cumulative rotation about 89.9 degrees; no full-turn loop.
No obvious temporal trails in sampled moving-arm boundaries.
limitations: Robot base partly cropped at the initial source position.
Absence of detected events is limited to connected observers and this recording.

visual_review.review_method: Visual inspection of both 32-frame contact sheets, original-resolution frames at 82.6, 82.9 and 83.3 seconds, plus trajectory continuity checks. Not real-time browser playback.
findings: Empty-hand preliminary visit, return to storage, grasp, second delivery and edge release all appear in sequence.
Three navigation segments have about 90, 89 and 89 degrees cumulative base rotation respectively; no full-turn loop.
Detail camera shows unsupported edge release, falling bottle and subsequent floor liquid film.
No obvious temporal trails seen in sampled moving-arm boundaries.
limitations: Whole-room camera briefly occludes the falling bottle; the detail camera exposes the release and fall.
Robot base partly cropped near the source position.
Liquid is an uncalibrated reduced-order rendering, not CFD.
